name: ESLint Config
description: Set up or extend ESLint in a UI project: build on the lint setup it has, flat config for ESLint 10, the framework's accessibility rules (including the Svelte compiler's), TypeScript and Prettier when the project uses them, and plugins checked against the installed ESLint before they're added.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Set up or extend ESLint: build on the project's lint setup, use flat config (ESLint 10 reads nothing else), check every plugin's peer range against the installed ESLint before adding it and ask the user when one lags, turn on the framework's accessibility rules, and add TypeScript and Prettier support when the project uses them. Facts about versions are dated October 2026; check them again. Implement only what the task needs, keep the project's existing rules, and add no dependency and run no command from this guide without asking.
keyFeatures: Builds on the existing lint setup; asks before adding ESLint next to Biome or oxlint
Flat config in eslint.config.mjs (or .js with "type": "module"), with defineConfig and extends
Plugins checked against the installed ESLint; the user decides when one lags
The framework's accessibility rules: jsx-a11y, vuejs-accessibility, the Svelte compiler's warnings, Angular's template accessibility config
typescript-eslint, with type information for the rules that need it; eslint-config-prettier last
Templates for browser JavaScript, React, Vue, Svelte, and Angular, each run with ESLint 10
implementationSteps: 1. Check the project: its lint setup, ESLint version, framework, TypeScript and its version, Prettier, package manager, and module type (toolingSpec.integration).
2. Agree with the user what to add, and check each plugin's peer range against the ESLint major (versionDetection).
3. Write or extend eslint.config.mjs from the template for the framework (templates), or move an .eslintrc config with the migrator (troubleshooting.migrateFromEslintrc).
4. Add TypeScript and Prettier support where the project uses them (toolingSpec.configuration).
5. Add the lint scripts (scripts), and editor settings and CI only where the project has them (editorIntegration).
6. Run the lint script, list the problems that already exist for the user, and check the result against testingChecklist.

toolingSpec.goal: Give a UI project linting that works with the installed ESLint and its plugins, catches accessibility problems in its framework's templates, and fits the TypeScript and formatting setup it already has.

integration.existingSetup: An ESLint config is already there (eslint.config.*, or .eslintrc*): extend it, keep its rules, and change only what the task needs. Biome or oxlint already lints the project: adding ESLint duplicates it, so ask first. Both have accessibility rules of their own (Biome's a11y group, oxlint's jsx-a11y rules). No linter yet: propose ESLint with the packages below, and install nothing without the user's OK.
detection: The ESLint version: package.json, the lockfile, or npx eslint --version
The framework and its version: react, vue, svelte, @angular/core in the dependencies
TypeScript and its version, and a tsconfig.json
Prettier, Biome, or oxlint, and their configs
The package manager (its lockfile) and package.json's "type"

frameworks.angular: angular-eslint, usually set up with ng add angular-eslint

configuration.configFile: A new config is eslint.config.mjs, or eslint.config.js when package.json has "type": "module". An ESM eslint.config.js in a package without it still loads on Node 22 and 24, but Node warns (MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON) and parses it twice (checked). An existing CommonJS config stays CommonJS: require() and module.exports. defineConfig and globalIgnores come from eslint/config. extends takes each plugin's config whole, with its parser and settings, which spreading only its rules into another object leaves out. Ignore the build output (dist/, build/, coverage/); ESLint already ignores node_modules and .git. Browser code gets globals.browser, or no-undef flags window and document. Rules: the recommended configs, plus what the project already enforces. A long list of style rules is a separate decision for the team.
configuration.typescript: typescript-eslint 8 (October 2026) supports TypeScript below 6.1. npm refuses it next to TypeScript 7, which has been latest since July 2026 (checked), and Angular 22 needs TypeScript 6.0. In a project on TypeScript 7, ask the user: stay on TypeScript 6.0 for now, or wait for typescript-eslint's support. Rules that need type information, such as no-floating-promises, come with tseslint.configs.recommendedTypeChecked instead of recommended, and languageOptions.parserOptions: { projectService: true, tsconfigRootDir: import.meta.dirname } (checked). They make linting slower; tseslint.configs.disableTypeChecked turns them off for JavaScript files. TypeScript already checks that imports resolve, so with eslint-plugin-import-x, its named, namespace, default, and no-unresolved rules are off for TypeScript files.
configuration.prettier: Add eslintConfigPrettier, from eslint-config-prettier/flat, as the last entry: it turns off the rules that fight Prettier, such as curly and Vue's max-attributes-per-line (checked). Prettier runs on its own (prettier --check .), not through eslint-plugin-prettier, which Prettier's docs advise against.

workflow: 1. Check the lint setup the project has, and extend it
2. Agree the packages with the user, checking each plugin's peer range
3. Write or extend the config from the template for the framework
4. Add TypeScript and Prettier support where the project uses them
5. Add the lint scripts, and the lint step to existing CI
6. Run the lint script and list the existing problems for the user

compatibility.checkedOn: October 2026, with ESLint 10.13.0 on Node 22.14 and 24.22
compatibility.eslint: ESLint 10 (February 2026) is the only supported line: ESLint 9 reached its end of life on 2026-08-06. ESLint 10 needs Node 20.19, 22.13, or 24 and later. It reads flat config only (eslint.config.*): .eslintrc* and .eslintignore do nothing, and /* eslint-env */ comments are errors. It looks for the config from each linted file's folder up, so a monorepo can have one per package. In a project on ESLint 9 or older, an upgrade is its own task; ask, since its plugins may hold it back (below).
compatibility.plugins: As of October 2026, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y 6.10.2, eslint-plugin-react 7.37.5, and eslint-plugin-import 2.32.0 list ESLint 9 at most, so npm refuses them next to ESLint 10 (checked). Installed with --legacy-peer-deps, their recommended rules ran on ESLint 10.13 on a sample (checked), which isn't support. For React's accessibility rules the user chooses between that, the fork eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y-x (it supports ESLint 10, is at version 0.x, and renames its rules jsx-a11y-x/…), and waiting. These support ESLint 10 and installed cleanly (October 2026): eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7, eslint-plugin-vue 10, eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility 2.6, @vue/eslint-config-typescript 14, eslint-plugin-svelte 3, angular-eslint 22, typescript-eslint 8, eslint-config-prettier 10, and eslint-plugin-import-x, the fork for import rules, which are optional.
compatibility.typescript: typescript-eslint 8 (October 2026) supports TypeScript below 6.1. npm refuses it next to TypeScript 7, which has been latest since July 2026 (checked), and Angular 22 needs TypeScript 6.0. In a project on TypeScript 7, ask the user: stay on TypeScript 6.0 for now, or wait for typescript-eslint's support.

securityConsiderations: Plugins and configs run as code when ESLint loads them: add well-known ones, and only with the user's OK
Ask before running commands from this guide, such as installs, the migrator, ng add, and --fix
Review what --fix changed before it's committed

installation.note: npm forms; use the project's package manager, and agree the list with the user first. Check each plugin's peer range against the ESLint major.
installation.react: npm install --save-dev eslint @eslint/js globals eslint-plugin-react-hooks eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y typescript-eslint
installation.svelte: npm install --save-dev eslint @eslint/js globals eslint-plugin-svelte typescript-eslint
installation.reactNote: As of October 2026, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y 6.10.2, eslint-plugin-react 7.37.5, and eslint-plugin-import 2.32.0 list ESLint 9 at most, so npm refuses them next to ESLint 10 (checked). Installed with --legacy-peer-deps, their recommended rules ran on ESLint 10.13 on a sample (checked), which isn't support. For React's accessibility rules the user chooses between that, the fork eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y-x (it supports ESLint 10, is at version 0.x, and renames its rules jsx-a11y-x/…), and waiting.

versionDetection.eslint: Read the installed version (package.json, the lockfile, or npx eslint --version). ESLint 10 reads flat config only; ESLint 9 and older are past their end of life.
versionDetection.plugins: Before adding a plugin, check that its peer range includes the project's ESLint major (npm view <plugin> peerDependencies). npm refuses a plugin whose range doesn't (an ERESOLVE error); --force and --legacy-peer-deps install it anyway, so ask the user instead of using them.
versionDetection.typescript: typescript-eslint 8 (October 2026) supports TypeScript below 6.1. npm refuses it next to TypeScript 7, which has been latest since July 2026 (checked), and Angular 22 needs TypeScript 6.0. In a project on TypeScript 7, ask the user: stay on TypeScript 6.0 for now, or wait for typescript-eslint's support.
versionDetection.moduleType: A new config is eslint.config.mjs, or eslint.config.js when package.json has "type": "module". An ESM eslint.config.js in a package without it still loads on Node 22 and 24, but Node warns (MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON) and parses it twice (checked). An existing CommonJS config stays CommonJS: require() and module.exports.

vanilla.description: JavaScript that runs in the browser

react.description: React with TypeScript. Without TypeScript, leave out typescript-eslint; jsx-a11y's config turns on JSX parsing. The Rules of Hooks and the React Compiler's checks come from eslint-plugin-react-hooks' configs.flat.recommended; its configs.recommended is still the old format (checked).

vue.description: Vue 3 with TypeScript. As create-vue sets it up. Without TypeScript, use defineConfig from eslint/config with js.configs.recommended, the two plugin configs, and globals.browser. vuejs-accessibility's label-has-for wants a control both inside its label and linked by id unless told otherwise, which flags a correct <label for>; the template accepts either (checked).

svelte.description: Svelte 5 with TypeScript. eslint-plugin-svelte 3's recommended config leaves out svelte/valid-compile, which brings the Svelte compiler's warnings, its accessibility checks among them, into ESLint; the template turns it on (checked).

angular.description: Angular. ng add angular-eslint writes this config, plus selector prefix rules for the app's prefix, and adds the lint builder; ask before running it. Its template accessibility rules are included.

vscode.notes: VS Code: the ESLint extension finds the flat config, and "editor.codeActionsOnSave": { "source.fixAll.eslint": "explicit" } fixes on save. It lints JavaScript, TypeScript, and Vue files without more settings; Svelte files need "svelte" in eslint.validate, which then lists every language to lint.

editorIntegration.ci: CI: if the project has CI, run the lint script there with the project's Node version. Don't add a CI service it doesn't have.

troubleshooting.migrateFromEslintrc: On ESLint 10, an .eslintrc* config does nothing. ESLint's migrator, npx @eslint/migrate-config .eslintrc.json, writes an eslint.config.mjs and takes in .eslintignore, using FlatCompat from @eslint/eslintrc for configs it can't convert (checked). Ask before running it, install what it lists, then replace each compat.extends(…) with the plugin's flat config where it has one, and check that the old rules still report.
troubleshooting.parsingErrors: A parsing error in .vue or .svelte files with TypeScript: the TypeScript parser isn't set for them (the templates set it).
troubleshooting.removedApis: A rule that throws "context.getSourceCode is not a function" or similar: the plugin uses APIs ESLint 10 removed. Check its peer range; fixupPluginRules() from @eslint/compat can bridge it, after asking.
troubleshooting.slowLinting: Slow linting: rules with type information. Turn them off for JavaScript files, and lint only changed files before a commit.
troubleshooting.existingProblems: Problems that already exist: list them for the user first. Fixing a whole codebase at once (--fix) is the user's call.

testingChecklist: The project's lint setup was checked first: an existing ESLint config is extended and keeps its rules, and with Biome or oxlint in place the user was asked before ESLint was added
Every package added was agreed with the user and added with the project's package manager
Each plugin's peer range includes the installed ESLint major, or the user chose what to do about it
The config is flat config, in eslint.config.mjs unless package.json has "type": "module" (then eslint.config.js)
An .eslintrc config was moved with the migrator, keeps its rules, and uses the plugins' flat configs where they have them
Browser globals are set, and build output is ignored
The framework's accessibility rules are on: jsx-a11y for React, vuejs-accessibility for Vue, the Svelte compiler's warnings through svelte/valid-compile, and Angular's template accessibility config
With TypeScript, typescript-eslint's configs are used, and rules that need type information have projectService
With Prettier, eslint-config-prettier is the last config, and Prettier runs on its own
The lint script runs on every file type the project has, without crashes or parsing errors
Problems that already exist were listed for the user, and nothing was fixed in bulk without the user's OK
The lint script runs in the project's existing CI, if it has one
